name: Opera Cake
description: A classic French rectangular layer cake — thin almond sponge, coffee syrup, and coffee buttercream stacked and finished with a mirror-glaze top.

layers.name: Joconde sponge (base)
layers.note: A thin almond flour sponge, baked in a sheet and cut to size — the structural foundation.

layers.name: Coffee syrup
layers.note: Brushed on generously so the thin sponge doesn't dry out under the weight of the layers above.

layers.name: Coffee buttercream
layers.note: A thin, even layer — spread too thick and it overwhelms the ganache.

layers.name: Chocolate ganache
layers.note: The rich middle layer that balances the coffee buttercream on either side.

layers.name: Joconde sponge
layers.note: A second sponge layer, keeping the cake's signature thin, even bands visible when sliced.

layers.name: Coffee syrup
layers.note: Soaks the second sponge layer the same way as the first.

layers.name: Coffee buttercream
layers.note: Mirrors the first buttercream layer for a balanced cross-section.

layers.name: Chocolate glaze (top finish)
layers.note: A poured, mirror-smooth glaze — the cake's signature glossy top, often finished with 'Opera' piped in chocolate.

name: Black Forest Cake
description: A German classic — dark chocolate sponge, cherries, and whipped cream, finished with chocolate shavings and a cherry on top.

layers.name: Chocolate sponge (base)
layers.note: A dark cocoa sponge layer, sturdy enough to support the cream and cherries above.

layers.name: Kirsch syrup
layers.note: A cherry-brandy soak brushed onto the sponge — the source of the cake's signature boozy note.

layers.name: Cherry filling
layers.note: Pitted cherries in a light syrup or compote, piled onto the soaked sponge.

layers.name: Whipped cream
layers.note: A generous layer piped or spread over the cherries, both a filling and part of the structural support.

layers.name: Chocolate sponge
layers.note: A second soaked sponge layer completing the stack.

layers.name: Whipped cream
layers.note: The full exterior coat — light and airy, unlike a dense buttercream finish.

layers.name: Chocolate decoration (top finish)
layers.note: Chocolate shavings or curls pressed onto the sides, with whipped cream rosettes and cherries on top.

name: Entremet
description: A modern French mousse cake, engineered in reverse in a mold — the glaze goes on last but sits on top of the finished dessert.

layers.name: Sponge (base)
layers.note: A thin, sturdy sponge (often joconde or genoise) that anchors the whole entremet.

layers.name: Crunch
layers.note: A thin layer of feuilletine or praline crunch — the textural contrast against the soft mousse above.

layers.name: Crémeux
layers.note: A dense, silky custard layer adding richness between the crunch and the insert.

layers.name: Insert
layers.note: A separately frozen component — often a fruit gelée or compote — that stays distinct once sliced.

layers.name: Mousse
layers.note: The dominant volume of the entremet, piped into the mold around the insert and crémeux, then frozen to set its shape.

layers.name: Glaze (top finish)
layers.note: Poured over the frozen, unmolded entremet — a mirror glaze or velvet spray gives the finished, glossy professional look.

name: Sachertorte
description: A dense Viennese chocolate cake — a single rich sponge split in two, sealed with apricot jam, and finished in a dark chocolate glaze.

layers.name: Chocolate sponge (base)
layers.note: A dense, flourless-leaning sponge made from melted chocolate, butter, and whipped egg whites — sturdy enough to slice clean in half.

layers.name: Apricot jam
layers.note: Warmed until spreadable and spread between the two sliced layers.

layers.name: Chocolate sponge
layers.note: The top half of the same split sponge, stacked back onto the jam.

layers.name: Apricot jam (seal coat)
layers.note: A thin coat brushed over the top and sides — this seals in crumbs and gives the glaze something smooth to cling to.

layers.name: Chocolate glaze (top finish)
layers.note: Warmed cream poured over chopped dark chocolate, then poured over the whole cake so it drips down the sides and sets glossy.

name: Kransekake
description: A Scandinavian celebration tower — graduated almond rings piped together with royal icing, with no cake layers or filling at all.

layers.name: Almond ring dough
layers.note: Almond flour, powdered sugar, and egg whites worked into a firm dough, then shaped into 18 graduated rings from largest to smallest.

layers.name: Baked rings
layers.note: Each ring baked separately in its mold until lightly golden, then cooled completely before stacking.

layers.name: Royal icing
layers.note: Egg white, powdered sugar, and lemon juice whisked to a stiff icing — piped in zigzags between each ring as the tower is stacked.

layers.name: Stacked tower (top finish)
layers.note: Rings stacked largest to smallest, icing zigzags left visible as the decoration — no separate frosting or filling layer.

name: Baumkuchen
description: A German 'tree cake' built entirely from its own batter — dozens of ultra-thin layers broiled on one after another until the tree-ring cross-section appears.

layers.name: Base batter layer
layers.note: A thin layer of butter-egg batter spread over the pan and broiled just until set and golden, 2-3 minutes.

layers.name: Repeated batter layers
layers.note: Another thin layer spread directly onto the previous one and broiled again — repeated 10-15 times, with no filling between layers, until the rings are built up.

layers.name: Apricot jam
layers.note: Brushed over the cooled, fully-layered cake once broiling is done.

layers.name: Chocolate glaze (top finish)
layers.note: An optional finishing glaze over the apricot coat — sliced crosswise, the cake reveals its signature visible tree rings.
